stories.headline: ‘Spider-Man,’ shirtless Tom Holland and why men are talking about ‘physique inflation’ - USA Today
stories.summary: Tom Holland's impressive physique in the new "Spider-Man" movie is getting applauded online. It's also prompted discussion about 'physique inflation.'
stories.why: Holland's visible muscularity represents escalating physical expectations for male action stars—what you're seeing on screen now requires year-round dedication that redefines 'fit' for your generation in ways previous Spider-Man actors didn't.

stories.headline: Disney agrees deal to let TikTokers use its films and TV shows in videos - BBC
stories.summary: A deal between will allow some creators to use clips from Disney films and TV shows in their videos.
stories.why: This signals the monetization of fandom itself; if you're a content creator, Disney's now paying for your ability to drive engagement through their IP, making parasocial entertainment creation a legitimate side income.

stories.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Triumph “Bodes Well” For ‘Avengers: Doomsday’, Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro Says - Deadline
stories.summary: Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro said Sony's record-setting opening of 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' "bodes well" for Disney's forthcoming 'Avengers' installment.
stories.why: Spider-Man's record opening validates Sony's gamble on standalone superhero films outside the MCU, meaning the next decade of blockbusters will prioritize franchise fragmentation over interconnected universes—changing what tentpoles you'll actually care about.

stories.headline: Six Slasher Movies That Gave Jane Schoenbrun's ‘Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’ Its Edge - GQ
stories.summary: Director Jane Schoenbrun on the slasher movies that inspired ‘Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,’ including ‘Friday the 13th’ sequels and two takes on Norman Bates.
stories.why: Schoenbrun's slasher inspiration matters because it marks elevated horror becoming a serious director's calling card, signaling that gory genre films are now respectable art cinema rather than guilty pleasures.

stories.headline: Once glamorous celebrity vacation hotspot is now overpriced and overrun with tourists and influencers: ‘Descended like locusts’ - New York Post
stories.summary: As Instagram, TikTok and luxury travel exploded in tandem, destinations once prized for exclusivity became valuable not just as vacation spots, but as backdrops.
stories.why: Instagram tourism destroying once-exclusive destinations reflects how social media algorithms democratized luxury travel, making your vacation spots commodified and crowded—the places that were exclusive five years ago are now Instagram checklist items.

stories.headline: Perez Hilton hospitalized after reports he livestreamed self-harm, sheriff’s officials say - NBC News
stories.summary: The blogger recently returned to his native Miami after living in Las Vegas.
stories.why: A former celebrity tabloid kingpin's public mental health crisis livestreamed represents how the attention economy that once made someone famous has now become the mechanism for their exploitation.

stories.headline: How Ariana Grande’s body became political - Salon.com
stories.summary: MAGA influencers want women not just thin, but weak
stories.why: Grande's body becoming a political symbol signals how fitness and thinness have become coded ideological statements in MAGA spaces, meaning what women's bodies represent culturally extends far beyond aesthetics into political identity warfare.

stories.headline: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis, charged with organizing the killing of Tupac Shakur, is on trial - NBC News
stories.summary: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis, who prosecutors say orchestrated the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, is going to trial almost 30 years after the fatal drive-by shooting in Las Vegas.
stories.why: Three decades after hip-hop's most iconic unsolved murder, actual prosecution finally arriving suggests cold cases involving Black victims are finally getting resources—this trial signals a cultural reckoning with decades of dismissed investigations.
